issues.detail: Rule condition uses prev_in (previous cycle input) but example's first row has no prior input; expected out=0 on first row is consistent only if prev_in initialized to 0, which is not stated.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next

issues.detail: Spec says capture 1->0 transitions; contract uses prev_in & ~in. Alternative semantics: capture any bit that is 0 in current cycle and was 1 in any earlier cycle (sticky until reset), not just immediate previous cycle.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next
issues.alternative: Set out[i] when in[i]==0 and out[i] was previously set or in[i] was 1 in any prior cycle since reset (i.e., detect any 0 after a 1, not only immediate 1->0).

issues.detail: R3_hold example shows out=0 throughout with in=1,3,1; no 1->0 transition occurs, so hold is consistent, but example does not demonstrate holding a previously set bit (out=1) as spec requires.
issues.spec_evidence: the output will remain 1 until the register is reset

issues.detail: R2 example: row1 in=0xFFFFFFFF, row2 in=0 -> out=0xFFFFFFFF on row2; row3 in=0 -> out stays 0xFFFFFFFF. Matches rule. No discrepancy.
Contract states update_during_reset=true and reset visible same_cycle; spec says active high synchronous reset, consistent. No verbatim evidence issue.
